Implementation Plan ## Implementation plan: `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_RESULT` per-attempt log line for OpenCode reviewer slots Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends reviewer_classify_retryable_failure Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one log-only line, and that is all this plan adds. Retry, failback, the circuit breaker, exit codes and slot outcomes stay the same. The new class function copies the rate-limit and server-error regexes and the watchdog and stall-state checks from `reviewer_classify_retryable_failure` (`scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:3921`), and adds the classes that function does not name. The line uses the same `printf ... | tee -a "${log_file}"` pattern as the existing `REVIEWER_CACHE:` and `REVIEWER_BACKOFF:` lines. The format matches the editor's `EDITOR_ATTEMPT_RESULT` line, so the two can be compared directly. Making the line builder a separate, testable function costs about 15 extra lines and no new dependency. It is the only way to test the model-sanitizing and no-stderr-leak requirements, so it is included. Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8094` at `5e87d2b7222ef72130f0fa735237ea0c1a4106fa`. This matches the integration branch metadata (mismatch: false). ## Files likely to change - `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` - `tests/test_review_reviewer_attempt_prompt_isolation.py` - `agents.d/-reviewer-attempt-result.md` (new; `` is this issue's number) - `changelog.d/-reviewer-attempt-result.md` (new) ## Functions or modules to implement The two new functions go in `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` directly after `reviewer_classify_retryable_failure`'s closing brace (line 3966), before `reviewer_log_advance_action`. This only adds lines, with no reflow and no renames. I checked that neither name exists anywhere in the repo yet. 1. **`reviewer_attempt_result_failure_class `** - Always returns 0 and prints exactly one class. - All arguments default to empty strings (`${1:-}` and so on), and `cmd_rc` is treated as `0` when it is not a number, so nothing fails under `set -e`/`set -u`. - It reads the no-text marker as a fixed string, `grep -Fqx 'OpenCode structured reviewer output contained no text events.'`, and only when `stderr_file` is set and the file is non-empty. - Classes are checked in this order: 1. `ok`: rc is 0 and the marker is absent. 2. `empty_structured_output`: the marker line is present. 3. `max_steps`: `wd_reason` is `max_steps`. 4. `stall_guard`: `stall_state` is `killed`. 5. `timeout`: `wd_reason` is `idle_timeout` or `max_wall`, or rc is 124, 137, 142 or 143. 6. `tool_repeat`: `wd_reason` is `tool_repeat`. 7. `rate_limit`: the classifier's exact regex `(^|[^0-9])429([^0-9]|$)|too many requests|rate limit` (`grep -Eiq`). 8. `server_error`: the classifier's exact 5xx regex, copied verbatim. 9. `provider_request_invalid`: `grep -Eiq '(http|status|status_code|code)[^0-9a-z]{0,16}400([^0-9]|$)|bad request|invalid_request'`, or the file contains both `reasoning.effort` and `max_tokens` (two `grep -Fq` checks). 10. `exit_nonzero`. - Note on step 5: rc 143 can only arrive here for `tool_repeat`/`max_steps` once those were already matched, because line 4382 forces `cmd_rc=143` for those watchdog reasons. Keeping the `tool_repeat` check after the rc check therefore matches the spec order. A forced 143 with `wd_reason=tool_repeat` and no stall classifies as `timeout`, exactly as the spec's ordering implies. This is recorded as D3. 2. **`reviewer_attempt_result_line `** - Prints exactly one line: `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_RESULT pass=

slot= attempt= model= exit_code= duration_secs= wd_reason= stall_state= failure_class=` - Sanitizing: - `model`: printed only when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$`, else `unknown`. - `pass`, `slot`, `wd_reason`: same token check, falling back to `unknown`, `unknown` and `none`. These are pipeline-derived, but they are checked anyway. - `attempt`, `exit_code`, `duration_secs`: must be all digits (`^[0-9]+$`), else `0`. A negative duration prints `0`. - `stall_state`: must be one of `observed` or `killed`, else `none`. - `failure_class`: must match `^[a-z_]+$`, else `exit_nonzero`. - Uses only `printf '%s'` with these values, in plain `case`/`[[ =~ ]]` tests. It never reads stderr, stdout or the prompt. 3. **Call site in `execute_reviewer_attempt`** (around line 4494). Directly after the `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_RETRYABLE_CLASS="$(reviewer_classify_retryable_failure ...)"` line and before the `if [ -n ... ]` that follows, add a small block: ``` reviewer_attempt_result_class="$(reviewer_attempt_result_failure_class "${cmd_rc}" "${wd_reason}" "${tmp_stderr}" "${stall_state}" 2>/dev/null || echo exit_nonzero)" reviewer_attempt_result_end="$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" # duration = end - start_time when both are numeric, else 0 reviewer_attempt_result_text="$(reviewer_attempt_result_line "${output_prefix:-}" "${safe_name:-}" "${attempt_number}" "${effective_model:-}" "${cmd_rc}" "" "${wd_reason}" "${stall_state}" "${reviewer_attempt_result_class}" 2>/dev/null || true)" then: if [ -n "${log_file:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$text" | tee -a "${log_file}" || true; else printf '%s\n' "$text"; fi ``` - Values come from what the function already has: - pass is `output_prefix`, set by `run_reviewer` and read through bash's dynamic scope; - slot is `safe_name`; - attempt is `attempt_number`; - model is `effective_model`; - the start time is the existing `start_time`, set at line 4204 just before launch, so no new start-time variable is needed; - stall state is `stall_state`, parsed at line 4387. - The new locals are `reviewer_attempt_result_class`, `reviewer_attempt_result_end`, `reviewer_attempt_result_duration` and `reviewer_attempt_result_text`, declared with the other `local`s at the top of `execute_reviewer_attempt` (around lines 4095–4115). None of these names exists today. - `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_RETRYABLE_CLASS`, `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_OUTCOME`, `cmd_rc` and every return path are left alone. - `run_pool_reviewer` (the Claude pool path) is not touched. ## Deferred scope None. This plan covers the whole issue, so the `## Deferred scope` section is not emitted. ## Data structures affected - No state, files, ledger fields or environment variables are added. - One new stdout/slot-log line. The slot log is `${PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR}/${output_prefix}_${safe_name}.log`, which is already uploaded as an artifact. ## API or interface changes - One new stable log prefix, `REVIEWER_ATTEMPT_RESULT`, registered through the agents.d fragment. - No CLI, workflow input, exit code or output-file changes. - `execute_reviewer_attempt` is called directly at line 4985, not inside `$(...)`, so the extra stdout line cannot corrupt a captured value. ## Decisions ### D1 — Emit only at the post-classifier point the issue names - Chosen: print the line only at the spot after `reviewer_classify_retryable_failure` (line 4494). - Alternatives considered: also print it on the success, silent-retry and PR-closed return paths (lines 4413–4450). - Why: The issue fixes this placement and says the change is log-only. Success, silent-retry and PR-closed attempts return earlier and print no line. In practice, `failure_class=ok` therefore means exit 0 with empty output and no no-text marker. The agents.d bullet will say so, so readers do not take `ok` to mean the slot succeeded. ### D2 — Separate pure line builder from the call site - Chosen: a `reviewer_attempt_result_line` helper that does all the sanitizing, plus a small block at the call site. - Alternatives considered: build the line inline with `printf` inside `execute_reviewer_attempt`. - Why: The tests must prove that unsafe model slugs print `unknown` and that the line never contains stderr. Testing that through `execute_reviewer_attempt` would require faking OpenCode. A pure helper can be pulled out with the existing `_extract_shell_function` pattern and run on its own. ### D3 — Follow the spec's class order exactly, including the forced rc 143 - Chosen: check timeout (rc 143) before `tool_repeat`, as the issue lists them. - Alternatives considered: check `tool_repeat` before the rc-based timeout, which is what the retryable classifier effectively does via its `wd_reason` case. - Why: The issue fixes the order. Line 4382 forces `cmd_rc=143` only when the rc was 0. A tool-repeat kill exits via SIGTERM, which is also 143, so either way it classifies as `timeout`. This is noted as a non-blocking warning. If the implementer wants `tool_repeat` to be reachable, the timeout step can be read as "`wd_reason` is `idle_timeout`/`max_wall`, or the rc is a timeout code and `wd_reason` is not `tool_repeat`". **Preferred:** apply the `wd_reason` check first so `tool_repeat` is reachable. That is a reading of the spec's intent ("`tool_repeat`" is listed as a class), and the test asserts `wd_reason=tool_repeat` with rc 143 gives `tool_repeat`. ### D4 — Anchor the HTTP 400 match to status context - Chosen: `(http|status|status_code|code)[^0-9a-z]{0,16}400([^0-9]|$)|bad request|invalid_request`. - Alternatives considered: a bare `(^|[^0-9])400([^0-9]|$)`. - Why: Reviewer stderr can contain line numbers or byte counts such as "400". It is still log-only, but a context anchor avoids misleading class labels. ## Security considerations - **Trust boundary:** OpenCode stderr and the provider responses inside it are untrusted. The class function only runs fixed `grep -F`/`-E` checks against the file and prints a token from a closed vocabulary. No stderr byte ever reaches the line. - **Injection and log-forgery:** model, pass, slot and wd_reason are token-checked against `[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]
